doc.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Bass solos and what the band plays behind them
summary: Caine laments the piano dropping out and the drummer going to hi-hat behind bass solos, and says swinging the band matters more than soloing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What about piano players who play on the low end an awful lot?

Well once again it depends. You know that’s the whole thing about rhythm section players: pianists, bass players and drummers, is we have to accompany, comp, and that’s just about being a good person and fitting in and being appropriate you know. It’s like you either have band players who play way too much or they don’t play at all. Like behind a bass solo I’m saying.
Behind a bass solo. Or, in general, it’s hard man.
When I hear a band and it’s time for the bass solo and everybody stops, that wouldn’t be my choice if I was the bass player.
I mean, why? I understand that you have to make room for sort of the low frequencies to be heard. But it’s almost like a cop out or something.

Yeah. You’re damn right. And then when you think about the fact that we spend our whole careers making everyone else sound good on their solos, and then we get our solo and the drummer goes to the hi-hat and the piano player like just fucking sits there. It’s infuriating to me.
What would you like to hear? Because well go ahead.

I can tell you what I’d like to hear. Well first of all, everyone’s different. I know some bass players who like the hi-hat. First of all you know why bass solos suck? Because there’s no bass behind them. I mean it’s so basic and so fucking simple. No one ever talks about it. There’s no bass behind us, so like if it’s a sax solo and he goes [scats] and then he doesn’t do anything, it’s moving forward, because I’m playing some hip shit hopefully. Now if I’m on a bass solo and I go [scats] nothing is going on. And the one person you want on the ride — he’s on the hi-hat. It’s like you motherfuckers go play with the hi-hat. Just you play the whole solo with the hi-hat and see how it goes, with no bass. You know it’s just fucking infuriating. So for me what I tell drummers to do is treat me like any other soloist, just be a little quieter. Like I like personally I like it when they’re on the ride and it’s a little cushion where I can have some space and it doesn’t die. But I’ve talked to a lot of great bass players who like the hi-hat thing. I really don’t like that. It’s too thin for me. It’s like I said there’s already no support ‘cause there’s no bass. A piano player who knows what the hell he’s doing — so at least let me get a ride cymbal.
Do you actually tell the drummer that?

Oh yeah. All the time. I’ll let them do what they do and then, and 80% of the time they do it because once again it’s some school shit. That’s what a bass solo’s for, I’ve got to go to a hi-hat because that’s what they taught me at Berklee in Room 111 you know or
whatever. It’s like no man, just play what feels right. And most of the drummers do that after I ask, just go switch to the ride, they’ll switch to the ride. It works out.

I appreciate your passion about that. I once remember writing a little blog about why are there all those bass player solo jokes. Like why? And I was sort of saying, I mean I understand what you’re saying like well everything disappears except for the one poor guy up there and now he’s got to carry the whole thing.
Yes. And I commit myself to making other people sound good. That’s what’s so frustrating about it. It’s funny actually. You’ve just got to laugh at it.
And, but usually you’re last, right?

Right. But I’ll say this, like bass solos are great and all, and I like to solo sometimes, and I enjoy a good bass solo, but that’s not how I judge a bass player. Like actually I really don’t care. I mean sometimes I do want to solo, but some nights I don’t want to solo at all. I mean my job is to swing the band. And you know that’s what a real bass player should take pride in. So if a guy can solo his ass off but he’s not swinging, he’s not playing good notes, he’s not doing his job. You know that’s not impressive to me.
